title: Local Filesystem State Flushing Under Load
pattern: Writing dynamic, high-frequency state updates as raw individual files on the local filesystem and calling `fsync()` under incoming traffic load.
why_bad: Forces random disk seeks and metadata updates (e.g., dentry cache allocation in the kernel). Under load, this exhausts OS memory, blocks request handling threads on mass storage I/O, and causes extremely long-tail latencies.
detection: Writing files to local directories in high-frequency loops or HTTP handler paths, especially when combined with `.sync_all()`.
counterexample: Writing low-frequency logs asynchronously or structured configuration writes during start/shutdown.
fix: Use a proper key-value database or database manager designed for sequential append-only writes.
source: *Building Secure and Reliable Systems*, p. 334; *Systems Performance*, p. 630-632.
